purpose: Development-only examples re-annotated from all v2.3 classification disagreements; never held-out evidence.
annotationPrinciple: Interaction mode, target coverage, diagnostic mechanism, reframe mechanism, and burden relation are separate judgments; no legacy class mechanically determines any v2.4 field.

examples.speaker: Sye Ten Bruggencate
examples.sourceExcerpt: you've admitted you could be a brain in a f I haven't admitted that I can be I haveed that I cannot prove that I'm not could that's right so therefore it follows that you could be the fact that something hasn't been proved to false does not mean that it's possible or true on what basis do you trust your senses and reasoning on their continued reliability at producing effective results

annotation.targetRationale: The act principally challenges the locked fallibilist distinction and the basis offered for relying on sense and reason.
annotation.coverageRationale: It converts inability to disprove the brain-in-a-vat scenario into the stronger modal claim that the scenario is possible, so it attacks a substitute instead of an indispensable component.
annotation.diagnosticRationale: The act asserts the disputed modal inference and asks for a basis; it does not identify a defect in the target and explain why that defect matters.
annotation.reframeRationale: It neither shows that the original demand is malformed nor states a corrected demand.
annotation.burdenRationale: The exchange is relevant to the transcendental case, but attacking a weaker modal claim does not materially advance the adopted dependence thesis.
annotation.legacyCaution: Do not relabel all contrary pressure as relevant-nonanswer; first test whether the act preserves the target's actual modal strength.

examples.speaker: Matt Dillahunty
examples.sourceExcerpt: if we agree that we must first presuppose the laws of logic then we shouldn't expand this potential Problem by presupposing something beyond the laws of logic we agree they're true when Sai claims that God serves as a foundation Beyond The Logical absolutes he's violating aam's Razer and when he claims that no other worldview can account for The Logical absolutes he needs to demonstrate the truth of this claim how did he do this has he done it

annotation.targetRationale: The act answers the demand for a foundation beyond logical absolutes and the assertion that only the Christian worldview can account for them.
annotation.coverageRationale: It addresses the extra-foundation demand by stopping at shared logical absolutes and addresses exclusivity by placing the missing comparative demonstration on its proponent.
annotation.diagnosticRationale: It identifies both an unsupported additional posit and a missing comparison, then explains why those omissions block the exclusivity claim.
annotation.reframeRationale: It explains why demanding a further foundation needlessly expands the shared starting point and substitutes the corrected comparative burden.
annotation.burdenRationale: The move materially advances the con side's central critique of the asserted Christian foundation, though the broader foundations case still requires defense.
annotation.legacyCaution: A move can be full coverage, diagnostic, and reframing at once; the legacy ordered class hid that coexistence.

examples.speaker: Matt Dillahunty
examples.sourceExcerpt: we live our lives by inference and induction we are under the general assumption that the future is going to be pretty much like the past not exactly like the past and that is because we have this trend of that always happening I'm not asserting that there is absolutely no difference in the future I'm saying that I believe and I believe that I am rationally justified in believing that the future is going to be pretty much like the past

annotation.targetRationale: The act principally answers the immediate request for the basis and strength of inductive expectation, not the separate later circularity diagnosis.
annotation.coverageRationale: It supplies the observed past trend and explicitly limits the conclusion to fallible broad continuity, covering the live request's basis and confidence components.
annotation.diagnosticRationale: It gives a positive basis without identifying a contradiction, missing premise, ambiguity, or invalid inference in the request.
annotation.reframeRationale: Narrowing one's own conclusion is calibration; the act does not explain that the opponent's demand itself is malformed.
annotation.burdenRationale: A fallibilist account of induction materially advances the con side's central defense of modest epistemic starting points.
annotation.legacyCaution: Do not infer reframe merely from qualification or a narrower conclusion; require an explained defect in the original demand.

examples.speaker: Unidentified audience members
examples.sourceExcerpt: is it possible that God has supplied you with a revelation that is at least in part false could God have lied to you about the path to heaven no and you know that yes God cannot lie is there any experience or set of experiences that would change your position no because if I were to doubt my position like I said doubt presupposes the existence of God reason presupposes God there is no no way that I could change a position because it's a necessary foundation for reason

annotation.targetRationale: The selected con act consists only of questions testing deception and corrigibility against the revelation route.
annotation.coverageRationale: The questions exert directly relevant pressure but do not themselves answer an indispensable component of the revelation claim; the opponent's replies in the mixed span are not part of the selected act.
annotation.diagnosticRationale: Questions that elicit clarification do not identify a defect and its consequence merely because the answers may later support one.
annotation.reframeRationale: The questions propose no corrected demand and give no account of why the original demand is malformed.
annotation.burdenRationale: They advance the subsidiary task of testing reliability and corrigibility, but do not yet establish the con side's defeating conclusion.
annotation.legacyCaution: Apply speaker ownership before annotation; never import an opponent's answer into the selected questioner's argumentative act.

examples.speaker: Sye Ten Bruggencate
examples.sourceExcerpt: that's a great question and it's a it's a huge misunderstanding of the argument I'm not saying logical absolutes or absolutes of any kind therefore God I'm saying You must start with the god of Christianity the only God exists that exists in order to make sense of any absolutes it's not absolutes therefore God it's God therefore absolutes

annotation.targetRationale: The act principally answers the immediate interpretation that the argument runs from absolutes to God.
annotation.coverageRationale: It expressly denies the reversed direction and states the intended God-to-absolutes direction, fully resolving the interpretive target even though broader exclusivity objections remain.
annotation.diagnosticRationale: It identifies a reversal of the intended inference and explains the corrected direction's relevance to understanding the argument.
annotation.reframeRationale: It treats the immediate question as malformed by reversal and supplies the corrected interpretive question and answer.
annotation.burdenRationale: Clarifying the direction is necessary to the transcendental burden but does not establish the dependence relation or Christian exclusivity.
annotation.legacyCaution: Keep the immediate interpretive target distinct from broader unresolved objections; full local coverage need not complete the burden.

examples.speaker: Sye Ten Bruggencate
examples.sourceExcerpt: that's the offer Jesus Christ or absurdity but you'll probably walk out of here choosing absurdity because because you love your sin but you know what your conscience is on my side you all know that God exists I urge you repent put your trust in Jesus Christ before it's too late because you will not like your eternity in hell

annotation.targetRationale: The closing principally restates the pro side's Christianity-or-absurdity thesis and exhortation rather than answering a particular live target.
annotation.coverageRationale: Coverage is not applicable to a constructive act.
annotation.diagnosticRationale: The act asserts a dilemma and audience motives without identifying and tracing a defect in a target inference.
annotation.reframeRationale: It does not correct a malformed opponent demand.
annotation.burdenRationale: The assertions concern the central topic, but without the missing dependence and discrimination bridges the exhortation does not materially advance the adopted burden.
annotation.legacyCaution: Interaction mode is functional, not chronological; a closing can be constructive, but central vocabulary alone does not guarantee central burden progress.

annotation.targetRationale: The act principally accepts and qualifies the proposed methodological package by requiring prior understanding of whole rival worldviews.
annotation.coverageRationale: The blanket acceptance reaches the stated virtues and the qualification explains how all of them should be applied in comparison.
annotation.diagnosticRationale: It recommends a methodological condition but does not identify a specific defect in the target's inference.
annotation.reframeRationale: It qualifies use of the proposed method without showing that the original demand is malformed or replacing it with a corrected one.
annotation.burdenRationale: The whole-worldview condition materially advances the con side's central comparison standard.
annotation.legacyCaution: Assent plus qualification can be responsive and full; it need not be treated as constructive merely because it also builds the speaker's method.

annotation.targetRationale: The act principally addresses the requested route from necessary existence and removed limits to supreme value and further attributes.
annotation.coverageRationale: It supplies the asserted value bridge and explains that the additional attributes are intended as implications of a simple base description; coverage does not require those derivations to be sound.
annotation.diagnosticRationale: It advances a positive derivation rather than identifying a defect in the target.
annotation.reframeRationale: It accepts the original demand and offers an answer rather than correcting the demand.
annotation.burdenRationale: The proposed bridge materially advances the central supreme-foundation case, although its warrants and downstream predictions remain incomplete.
annotation.legacyCaution: Separate structural coverage from evidential adequacy; a thin answer can still touch every indispensable component.

annotation.targetRationale: The act answers a challenge asking both what the claimed predictions are and why they follow from supreme value.
annotation.coverageRationale: It supplies a concrete list of alleged predictions but not the indispensable entailment or warrant linking them to supreme value.
annotation.diagnosticRationale: Listing proposed consequences identifies no defect in the target reasoning.
annotation.reframeRationale: The response accepts rather than repairs the original demand.
annotation.burdenRationale: Concrete predictions are a necessary subsidiary component of the unification burden, but the missing derivation prevents central completion.
annotation.legacyCaution: Concrete content answers a what-question, not automatically the why-it-follows component of a compound target.

annotation.targetRationale: The act principally responds to the available epistemic options about the initial state and, more broadly, the claimed supreme-value consequences.
annotation.coverageRationale: It selects suspension and gives present scientific ignorance as its basis, but it does not address the no-limits rationale or the individual claimed consequences.
annotation.diagnosticRationale: An assertion of limited access is not by itself an identified defect in the opponent's inference with an explained consequence.
annotation.reframeRationale: It answers the epistemic-choice demand directly rather than replacing a malformed demand.
annotation.burdenRationale: Suspension grounded in evidential limits materially advances the con side's central epistemic-restraint burden.
annotation.legacyCaution: Relevant contrary material becomes partial coverage only when it resolves at least one preidentified indispensable component.

annotation.targetRationale: The act principally answers whether necessity terminates all explanation by separating existence from explanation of necessary features.
annotation.coverageRationale: It concedes that necessity ends the contingency-style existence question and supplies deeper explanation among necessary truths for the remaining feature question.
annotation.diagnosticRationale: It identifies an ambiguity between explaining existence and explaining properties and shows why the distinction changes the stopping claim.
annotation.reframeRationale: It explains why the contingency-style existence demand is misplaced and states the corrected demand concerning necessary features.
annotation.burdenRationale: The distinction materially advances the pro side's central explanatory project, while substantive derivations of the features remain.
annotation.legacyCaution: Under orthogonal annotation, reframe and diagnosis do not displace full coverage when the corrected demand is also answered.

annotation.targetRationale: The act is offered against the immediately preceding proposal that necessary features may admit deeper explanation.
annotation.coverageRationale: Future-physics caution is relevant to whether the project is presently warranted but does not address the conceptual distinction between necessary existence and explanation of necessary features.
annotation.diagnosticRationale: It reports evidential ignorance without locating a contradiction, missing premise, ambiguity, or invalid inference in the conceptual claim.
annotation.reframeRationale: It neither declares the explanatory demand malformed nor supplies a corrected demand.
annotation.burdenRationale: Present ignorance materially advances the con side's central epistemic-restraint case even though it does not answer this conceptual target.
annotation.legacyCaution: Coverage and burden relation answer different questions: a relevant nonanswer can still advance the speaker's adopted central burden.

annotation.targetRationale: The act principally answers the proposed nonphysical and partly a priori route beyond scientific inquiry.
annotation.coverageRationale: Causal continuity addresses why the initial physical state remains a scientific subject, and the historical objection addresses the reliability of the general a priori route without enumerating every example.
annotation.diagnosticRationale: It identifies the poor historical reliability of imposing a priori constraints and explains why that undermines confidence in the proposed route.
annotation.reframeRationale: It contests the route's reliability rather than replacing a malformed demand.
annotation.burdenRationale: The response materially advances the con side's central resistance to adding unsupported attributes to the initial reality.
annotation.legacyCaution: Full coverage of a general claim does not require item-by-item replies when one stated reason applies to all indispensable instances.

annotation.targetRationale: The act principally answers the immediate challenge to the benefit and feasibility of a deeper unifying foundation.
annotation.coverageRationale: The mathematical-axiom analogy supplies the alleged unification benefit but does not show that logic, value, or mind can actually be derived from the causal foundation.
annotation.diagnosticRationale: An analogy offering a positive benefit does not identify a defect in the target inference.
annotation.reframeRationale: It accepts and only partly answers the original challenge.
annotation.burdenRationale: A unification analogy advances a necessary subsidiary issue, but the central derivation remains unsupported.
annotation.legacyCaution: An empty legacy target set does not make a responsive act constructive when the immediate live claim is evident from context.

annotation.targetRationale: The act principally answers both the claimed epistemic support and explanatory benefit of mathematical-style axiomatization.
annotation.coverageRationale: It answers the epistemic-support component by reversing the direction of justification but leaves the distinct explanatory-unification component unresolved.
annotation.diagnosticRationale: It identifies a reversed direction of warrant and explains why neat axiomatization alone cannot independently support the theory.
annotation.reframeRationale: It rejects an inference rather than explaining that the demand itself is malformed and replacing it.
annotation.burdenRationale: The diagnosis advances a necessary subsidiary part of the total-worldview comparison but does not complete the con side's application of that standard.
annotation.legacyCaution: A successful diagnosis of one component remains diagnostic true while compound target coverage stays partial.

annotation.targetRationale: The act principally answers the introspection-based irreducibility challenge and its dependent mind-first inference.
annotation.coverageRationale: It separates introspective content from metaphysical identity and supplies behavioral, animal, and neural-insult evidence for identity theory, reaching both indispensable components.
annotation.diagnosticRationale: It identifies introspection's inability to discriminate metaphysical identity and explains why independent abductive evidence must decide the issue.
annotation.reframeRationale: It answers the original evidential dispute without declaring its demand malformed.
annotation.burdenRationale: If successful, the act states the identity view's evidential basis, neutralizes introspection as a discriminator, and thereby satisfies the locked con consciousness burden.
annotation.legacyCaution: A move may complete an adopted burden even when its precise strongest target was not represented by a legacy selected ID.

annotation.targetRationale: The act principally answers the identity claim by distinguishing token-event identity from property-level difference.
annotation.coverageRationale: It supplies the substantive account under which one event can be identical while instantiating apparently distinct properties, reaching the decisive identity component.
annotation.diagnosticRationale: It identifies a type/token ambiguity and explains how resolving it blocks the inference from event identity to property identity.
annotation.reframeRationale: It clarifies a distinction inside the original dispute rather than replacing a malformed demand.
annotation.burdenRationale: The distinction advances the necessary irreducibility sub-burden, but it does not establish the further comparative mind-first conclusion.
annotation.legacyCaution: Diagnostic true does not require coverage below full; a diagnosis can itself furnish a complete substantive answer.

annotation.targetRationale: The act principally develops the con side's whole-worldview comparison standard in response to a moderator prompt, not an adopted opponent claim.
annotation.coverageRationale: Coverage is not applicable to a constructive act.
annotation.diagnosticRationale: The local-advantage warning illustrates the speaker's positive standard, but no live target defect is identified and traced in the selected act.
annotation.reframeRationale: It develops a method rather than repairing a malformed opponent demand.
annotation.burdenRationale: The total-commitments standard materially advances the central con comparison burden, although it still must be applied to both worldviews.
annotation.legacyCaution: Do not infer a responsive diagnosis from generic criticism when the criticized inference is not a live adopted target.

examples.speaker: Jessica Frazier
examples.sourceExcerpt: There's whatever creates the world. If you're a Thomist, they're the powers in God, the concepts in God that unfold and generate. And then there's the parts of God which are under it. And if you're a physicist, there's the Big Bang and the whatever it is that's generating space-time.

annotation.targetRationale: The act principally answers the moderator's live request for the alternative account's explanatory level and viability.
annotation.coverageRationale: It identifies generative powers or a supporting condition, but does not explain enough to establish that ground as a viable alternative to classical creation.
annotation.diagnosticRationale: It offers positive comparative content without identifying a defect in the target.
annotation.reframeRationale: It accepts the explanatory request rather than correcting it.
annotation.burdenRationale: Specifying a generative level advances a necessary subsidiary component of the impersonal alternative, but the explanatory route remains incomplete.
annotation.legacyCaution: Moderator claims and demands can be genuine response targets even when the legacy inventory contains no target ID.

examples.speaker: William Lane Craig
examples.sourceExcerpt: There's a creator-creation distinction since the creation is material in space and time, but the creator is an immaterial, spiritual, transcendent reality that has brought the physical world into being. In this case, we would want to say, I think, that God is what you've called a self-natured being.

annotation.targetRationale: The act principally answers the comparison between a generative ground and classical creation.
annotation.coverageRationale: It supplies the requested differentiating ontology: immaterial creator versus material creation, transcendent versus spatiotemporal, and necessary versus contingent.
annotation.diagnosticRationale: It states a rival ontology rather than identifying a defect in the target argument.
annotation.reframeRationale: It answers the comparison on its stated terms.
annotation.burdenRationale: The creator-creation distinction supports a necessary subsidiary reply, but it does not itself give the full route from physical reality to a personal creator.
annotation.legacyCaution: Coverage of a local comparison can be full while burden progress remains subsidiary.

examples.speaker: Jessica Frazier
examples.sourceExcerpt: Emanationism gets given lots of different ontological sort of play outs, right? I mean, even Aquinas will say creation ex nihilo never means that God creates the world and then he's like, ‘That was great. I'm going away.’ In fact, that was a heresy. The universe, all that the divine creates, is always sustained.

annotation.targetRationale: The act principally challenges the categorical contrast between classical creation and emanation.
annotation.coverageRationale: Continuous sustaining is relevant contrary material but does not answer the target's necessary/contingent, immaterial/material, or creation-by rather than creation-out-of distinctions.
annotation.diagnosticRationale: It does not identify a defect in those stated property distinctions and trace a defeating consequence.
annotation.reframeRationale: It supplies a related comparison without correcting a malformed demand.
annotation.burdenRationale: The sustaining point advances a subsidiary challenge to the contrast, but it does not yet establish the alternative's ontology.
annotation.legacyCaution: Topic overlap is not partial coverage unless at least one indispensable target component is actually addressed.

examples.speaker: Philip Goff
examples.sourceExcerpt: Think of a Venn diagram where you've got the bit of God that's wholly other, that's completely separate from the universe; the bit of the universe or the nature of the universe which is wholly separate to God; and then the bit in the middle, like a Venn diagram.

annotation.targetRationale: The act principally opposes the strict creator-creation separation with an overlap model.
annotation.coverageRationale: The rival Venn model is relevant but does not answer any stated modal or material reason for the separation in this selected act.
annotation.diagnosticRationale: It asserts an alternative without identifying why a premise or inference in the target fails.
annotation.reframeRationale: It changes the proposed ontology but does not explain that the original demand is malformed.
annotation.burdenRationale: Introducing overlap advances a necessary subsidiary component of the limited-God alternative, but its compatibility is not yet defended.
annotation.legacyCaution: Denying a conclusion is not partial coverage when the act has not engaged an indispensable reason offered for that conclusion.

examples.speaker: Philip Goff
examples.sourceExcerpt: I wouldn't define the physical universe as essentially contingent then. I think most of it is, but I think there's something at the core of the universe, there's something at the core of you, Bill, and at the core of me that is necessary, timeless, uncreated. And that's where the overlap is.

annotation.targetRationale: The act principally answers the alleged contradiction between the universe's contingency and overlap with a necessary divine reality.
annotation.coverageRationale: It denies that every part of the universe is contingent and locates overlap only in a necessary, timeless, uncreated core, resolving the premise that generates the contradiction.
annotation.diagnosticRationale: It identifies the overgeneralized contingency premise and explains why removing it dissolves the contradiction.
annotation.reframeRationale: It defeats a premise within the original objection rather than replacing the demand.
annotation.burdenRationale: Removing the contradiction materially advances the central limited-God alternative, though the necessary core still requires independent support.
annotation.legacyCaution: Diagnosis and full coverage can coincide; do not force an exclusive choice between mechanism and contact.

examples.speaker: Philip Goff
examples.sourceExcerpt: Neurophysiologically, what it looks like it's doing is suppressing, stopping neural activity, not creating new neural activity like you imagine in a hallucination. Imagine my mind is a light bulb wrapped in cotton wool. The cotton wool is what's particular to me, Philip Goff, and the light bulb is this pure consciousness.

annotation.targetRationale: The act principally answers the immediate drug-causation objection that altered neural activity fabricates rather than discloses experience.
annotation.coverageRationale: It distinguishes neural suppression from hallucinatory production and supplies a filter model explaining how suppression could disclose consciousness.
annotation.diagnosticRationale: The act offers a competing mechanism but does not identify a formal defect in the target's inference and its consequence.
annotation.reframeRationale: It answers the causal challenge directly rather than correcting its demand.
annotation.burdenRationale: The disclosure model materially advances the central consciousness-involving alternative, while its evidential warrant remains contested.
annotation.legacyCaution: A response can have an empty legacy target set yet still be full coverage of a clear immediately preceding objection.

examples.speaker: William Lane Craig
examples.sourceExcerpt: Once one starts appealing to these sorts of mystical experiences to justify your worldview, it seems to me that you've lost all controls on objectivity and on truth. I too could claim what you would probably call a mystical experience, namely, at the age of sixteen, after six months of the most intense soul-searching I've ever been through, I was spiritually born again.

annotation.targetRationale: The act principally challenges both the drug-event interpretation and the broader inference from mystical experience to Goff's worldview.
annotation.coverageRationale: It addresses the worldview-warrant component through underdetermination and rival experience but does not answer the neural-suppression or filter-mechanism component.
annotation.diagnosticRationale: It identifies a missing objective discriminator among incompatible experiential interpretations and explains why that gap blocks the worldview-level inference.
annotation.reframeRationale: It demands controls for the existing inference rather than explaining that the demand is malformed and replacing it.
annotation.burdenRationale: The discrimination challenge materially advances the pro side's central epistemic-control burden, though its own public discriminator is not yet supplied.
annotation.legacyCaution: A diagnosis that defeats one inferential component does not make coverage full when the target packet contains a separate causal component.

examples.speaker: Philip Goff
examples.sourceExcerpt: You can't get outside of your consciousness and check whether it's corresponding to reality. So, what do you do? You've just got to decide which experiences seem most evident. And anybody who's had the experience I had—it is more compelling than anything in ordinary experience, far more compelling. Also, with this particular substance, it is very uniform.

annotation.targetRationale: The act principally answers the demand for objective controls and a discriminator among rival experiential interpretations.
annotation.coverageRationale: It offers intensity and cross-person uniformity as internal comparative evidence but does not answer the rival Christian interpretation or the proposed historical discriminator.
annotation.diagnosticRationale: The impossibility of stepping outside consciousness targets direct correspondence checking, not the indirect controls actually requested, so the required relevance to the target defect is absent.
annotation.reframeRationale: It does not show that indirect objective controls are malformed and therefore fails the strict two-part reframe test.
annotation.burdenRationale: Comparative experiential features advance a necessary subsidiary evidential issue, but they do not complete the alternative's discriminating inference.
annotation.legacyCaution: Do not credit a reframe aimed at a stronger demand than the opponent made; test the corrected demand against the actual target.

examples.speaker: Jessica Frazier
examples.sourceExcerpt: You might have to speak to experiences that go beyond the usual. The first time as a kid I experienced what it was like when the plane dives and you feel weightlessness, it was a new experience. It didn't mean it was not a veridical experience. It was just an unusual thing.

annotation.targetRationale: The act principally answers the claim that unusual phenomenology lacks cognitively usable or veridical content.
annotation.coverageRationale: The analogy addresses whether unfamiliar experience can be veridical but does not establish publicly assessable content or discriminate its metaphysical interpretation.
annotation.diagnosticRationale: It supplies an analogy rather than identifying a contradiction, missing premise, ambiguity, or invalid inference in the target.
annotation.reframeRationale: It answers one component of the existing challenge without correcting the demand.
annotation.burdenRationale: Defending possible veridicality advances a necessary subsidiary issue for the experience-based alternative, but the public inference remains open.
annotation.legacyCaution: Lock the principal immediate target; broader earlier control objections may remain context without becoming coequal target components.

examples.speaker: William Lane Craig
examples.sourceExcerpt: I'm talking about meaning in an objective sense, not a subjective sense. Is there an objective meaning to human existence? And it seems to me to have an objective meaning, we need this external transcendent reality, God, to tell us what the objective meaning in life is. The meaning of life is to glorify God and to know him and enjoy him forever.

annotation.targetRationale: The act principally answers the ambiguity challenge about meaning and God's proposed relation to objective purpose.
annotation.coverageRationale: It distinguishes objective from subjective meaning and identifies both the transcendent source and content of the claimed objective purpose.
annotation.diagnosticRationale: Clarifying the intended sense answers an ambiguity but does not identify a defect in the opponent's inference and explain its defeating relevance.
annotation.reframeRationale: It specifies the sense under dispute without claiming that the opponent's demand is malformed or substituting a corrected demand.
annotation.burdenRationale: The grounding account materially advances the central pro meaning burden, while comparative and authority objections remain.
annotation.legacyCaution: Ordinary disambiguation is not automatically a justified reframe; require an explicit malformed-demand diagnosis plus a corrected demand.

examples.speaker: Jessica Frazier
examples.sourceExcerpt: Hinduism says there are moral structures. If you're in the world and you're a consciousness and you're interacting with other consciousness, you have moral responsibilities. And since you are and I am and we all are here, we have those responsibilities. Hinduism is extremely invested in understanding what's called dharma, the structure of how the world around us works.

annotation.targetRationale: The act principally answers a live characterization that optional spiritual liberation leaves Hinduism without moral responsibility.
annotation.coverageRationale: It distinguishes optional spiritual trajectory from duties among interacting conscious beings and supplies dharma as the moral structure, covering the characterization's components.
annotation.diagnosticRationale: It identifies a conflation between optional liberation and interpersonal obligation and explains why the conflation misstates the alternative.
annotation.reframeRationale: It explains why the original characterization confuses two questions and answers the corrected responsibility question through dharma.
annotation.burdenRationale: The alternative moral structure materially advances the central con burden against classical-theist exclusivity, though its grounding remains to be defended.
annotation.legacyCaution: A target need not have a legacy selected-move ID; an unselected moderator characterization can still support full, diagnostic, and reframe annotations.

examples.speaker: Joe Folley
examples.sourceExcerpt: The mere objectivity of value seems to be underselling the strength of theism here. The Platonic good is a little bit toothless. The advantage of theism isn't necessarily in the mere objectivity of values. It's in the presence of an enforcer of values. That doesn't have anything to do with objectivity at all.

annotation.targetRationale: The act principally develops Folley's positive distinction between objective value and agential enforcement after an open invitation for his view.
annotation.coverageRationale: Coverage is not applicable to a constructive act.
annotation.diagnosticRationale: The contrast helps build the speaker's theory but is not tied to a live opponent target defect and consequence.
annotation.reframeRationale: An open moderator prompt is not a malformed demand requiring correction.
annotation.burdenRationale: The objectivity/enforcement distinction materially advances the central con analysis of what theism adds to normativity.
annotation.legacyCaution: Do not treat every newly drawn distinction as a reframe; first determine whether there is a live opponent demand being repaired.

examples.speaker: Philip Goff
examples.sourceExcerpt: David Hume has this idea that all fundamental life goals are on a par. Reason is the slave of the passions. I just think that can't be true. Imagine someone whose fundamental life goal is counting blades of grass, and they don't enjoy it, they get no pleasure from it. That's just their fundamental life goal.

annotation.targetRationale: The act principally answers the compound claim that divine command is needed for objective evaluative hierarchy and obligation.
annotation.coverageRationale: The grass-counting example contests the evaluative-hierarchy component without explaining how objective hierarchy generates duties or replacing qualified authority.
annotation.diagnosticRationale: The counterexample presses one claim but does not identify a formal defect and its broader consequence for the compound inference.
annotation.reframeRationale: It accepts the evaluative dispute rather than correcting its demand.
annotation.burdenRationale: Objective hierarchy without divine command advances a necessary subsidiary challenge, but the value-to-duty bridge remains unresolved.
annotation.legacyCaution: A substantive counterexample is partial only when it contacts an indispensable component; its failure to reach another component must remain visible.

examples.speaker: William Lane Craig
examples.sourceExcerpt: What happens when your moral duty contradicts what prudence tells you to do? Self-interest and morality often come head-on into conflict. Theism provides a basis for doing your moral duty even at the expense of self-interest, and therefore following your moral obligations over your prudential interests. That's one more practical argument in support of a theistic perspective.

annotation.targetRationale: The act principally answers the claim that theism's moral force reduces to prudential enforcement and the related question of objective status.
annotation.coverageRationale: It distinguishes duty from self-interest and says theism supports choosing duty, but it does not answer what objectivity contributes or supply the full positive authority bridge.
annotation.diagnosticRationale: It offers a counterdistinction without identifying a defect and tracing why that defect defeats the target reasoning.
annotation.reframeRationale: It answers part of the original challenge rather than replacing a malformed demand.
annotation.burdenRationale: The duty/prudence distinction materially advances the central pro normativity burden, though grounding and authority remain underdeveloped.
annotation.legacyCaution: Compressed support may affect later numerical quality, but missing target components still make structural coverage partial.
